column3: NASB follows the critical text, without “and”; “illuminated from” is rendered “illumined with.”
NASB follows the critical text (“mighty voice,” “demons”), but it does not include the critical text’s “a prison of every unclean beast.” “Habitation” is rendered “dwelling place.”
NASB follows the critical text (“have drunk”); “wrath” is rendered “passion,” and “power” “wealth.”
“Have fellowship” is rendered “participate.”
NASB follows the critical text (“piled up”).
NASB follows the critical text (without “you”); “render” is rendered “paid,” and “mix double” “mix twice as much.”
NASB follows the critical text; “misery” is rendered “mourning,” and NASB puts the quotation partly in capitals.
“Death” is rendered “pestilence,” and “misery” “mourning.”
NASB follows the critical text; it reorders the clause.
“From afar” is rendered “at a distance.”
NASB follows the critical text; “cargo” is rendered “cargoes.”
NASB follows the critical text; “all citron wood” is rendered “every kind of citron wood.”
NASB follows the critical text (“and spice”); “myrrh” is rendered “perfume,” “souls of men” “human lives,” and NASB supplies “cargoes of.”
NASB follows the critical text (“men will no longer find them”); “the ripe fruit of the desire of your soul” is rendered “the fruit you long for.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it supplies “she who was.”
NASB follows the critical text (“every passenger”); “brought to desolation” is rendered “laid waste,” and “trade by the sea” “make their living by the sea.”
NASB follows the critical text (“as they saw”); “What is like the great city?” is rendered “What city is like the great city?”
NASB follows the critical text; “desolated” is rendered “laid waste.”
NASB follows the critical text (“and you saints and apostles”); “did judge the judgment for you” is rendered “has pronounced judgment for you.”
NASB follows the critical text (“great millstone”); “one angel” is rendered “a strong angel,” moving “mighty.”
“Millstone” is rendered “mill.”
NASB supplies “men.”
NASB follows the critical text (“blood”).
